newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle up $1 at $66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle up $1 at $66 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were actively trading at $66.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from the bulk of last week's sales, feedlot sources said.
About 15,000 to 30,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 15,000 in Kansas, they said. Buying turned active shortly before midday, the feedlot sources said.

Fed cattle price advances were powered by strong post-Christmas packer demand, they said. Demand for cattle for a large slaughter schedule to make up for holiday closings also underpinned prices, the sources said.
Strong retail demand was expected for planned beef features the first two weeks of January.
Tight beef supplies because of holiday-shortened production this week and next also lent support on ideas that beef prices would be firm, market sources said.
Beef prices Tuesday were quoted up $0.16 to $0.80 per cwt, with 95 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
